source.title: A DNN Optimizer that Improves over AdaBelief by Suppression of the Adaptive Stepsize Range
source.authors: Guoqiang Zhang; K. Niwa; W. Kleijn

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices, though the final pages include garbled figure/OCR content.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and step-size-range measurements that refine V4, including task-dependent results where the proposed adaptive optimizer beats or matches alternatives. It does not test memorization/generalization gaps as framed by the other versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s optimizer interventions and the measured adaptive-step-size ranges, which bear on V4. Comparisons cited from prior work are excluded. Validation metrics are reported as results, but the paper does not report training performance alongside them, so they do not establish a training-versus-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out comparisons of established adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on image and language tasks, bearing on V4. Its tuning includes epsilon searches, so it does not reproduce the learning-rate-and-schedule-only condition. Aida-versus-AdaBelief improvements and step-size statistics do not themselves test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors attribute Aida's generally better validation performance to compressed adaptive-step-size ranges, report competitive WGAN-GP performance and a small ImageNet improvement over AdaBelief, and describe SGD as competitive chiefly on VGG and ResNet. These are the authors' conclusions, not evidence that adaptive methods generally underperform SGD.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes Aida, an extension of AdaBelief using mutual layerwise vector projections and evaluates optimizer performance. It does not test the original claim's memorization and train-test-gap setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Task/model and Aida projection count K affect reported performance; K=2 generally exceeds K=1. Adaptive-step-size range changes with the epsilon placement and projection count. The paper reports tuned discrete parameter searches for comparison optimizers on some tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Epsilon placement and Aida's projections compress adaptive-step-size ranges and standard deviations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer update design controls the distribution of adaptive step sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Aida improves reported validation metrics relative to AdaBelief across the listed classification and language tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed Aida optimizer improves on AdaBelief under the evaluated recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: WGAN-GP's selected best FID is 55.7 for Aida K=2 and 56.73 for AdaBelief.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects the best observed image-generation FID under configuration searches.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), as stated in supplied metadata; paper text does not state the venue.
record.problems: The paper reports validation accuracy or perplexity, not paired training-versus-test metrics, so it does not directly measure the generalization gap. Some comparisons omit standard deviations or uncertainty; Table II explicitly omits standard deviations. ImageNet compares only Aida with AdaBelief. WGAN-GP reports best FID across configurations without uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Figure 1's adaptive-step-size averages are described qualitatively but largely lack numeric values; the more directly stated Figure 3 comparison and the stated Figure 2 standard-deviation finding are retained. Table IV's other optimizer entries are not separately listed because V4 concerns the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison and the authors summarize Aida as matching the best in that task.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

The strict learning-rate-and-decay-schedule-only tuning condition; a controlled narrow-versus-broad tuning comparison; equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance relative to SGD; switching from Adam to SGD; and a controlled demonstration that decoupled weight decay recovers a deficit.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Established adaptive-versus-SGD image-classification comparisons, including all four Adam/SGD pairs and adaptive-method variation. Adam accuracies are 91.20±0.21, 95.09±0.18, 67.88±0.13, and 77.31±0.14; corresponding SGD accuracies are 91.36±0.07, 95.48±0.11, 67.02±0.25, and 78.10±0.18. Record epsilon searches and fixed learning rates as conditions.
missing.locator: Table III; Section IV.C; Appendix E, Table X

missing.what: Adam-versus-SGD Penn TreeBank comparisons for each LSTM depth: perplexity 84.28 versus 85.52, 66.86 versus 67.44, and 64.28 versus 63.68. Record the learning-rate and epsilon searches. These comparisons are not captured by the Aida/AdaBelief rows.
missing.locator: Table II; Section IV.B; Appendix E, Table VIII

missing.what: Complete R4 with established adaptive comparators, especially Adam 64.71±0.57, and their tuning conditions. Adaptive methods do not uniformly beat SGD: Fromage and MSVAG score 35.57±0.19 and 53.79±0.13.
missing.locator: Table I; Section IV.A; Appendix E, Table VII

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket statement that training performance is unreported is incorrect: Figure 5 includes Transformer training perplexity for Adam, AdaBelief, and Aida. It does not include SGD, so it cannot establish the training-performance clause of the adaptive-versus-SGD claim. Better Aida performance than AdaBelief is not support for V4, and unavailable training metrics are untested rather than scope limitations.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization to natural labels.

The paper compares Aida with adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers; it does not test the full range of tuning regimes, explicit switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay as a recovery mechanism, or language-model Adam advantages as framed in the version.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting accuracy change.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.operation_detail: Compared layerwise average adaptive-step-size ranges for Adam, AdaBelief, AdaBelief*, and Aida at K=1 and K=2 during CIFAR10 training.
rows.measure: Range of eleven layerwise average adaptive step sizes
rows.baseline: AdaBelief: ten of eleven values close to 320
rows.locator: Section II, Figure 3 and accompanying text
rows.note: AdaBelief* removes the first epsilon from the AdaBelief second-momentum computation; this comparison concerns step-size range, not a measured train-test gap.
rows.check: Step-size ranges do not measure held-out performance relative to SGD. The reported numbers are consistent with the text.

source_check.locator_found: Section II, Figure 3 and accompanying paragraph

rows.note: Adam+ adds epsilon in the computation of its second-moment estimate.
rows.check: Step-size compression alone cannot establish V4's performance comparison.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer validation accuracy over training.
rows.note: The paper reports validation accuracy, not the paired training accuracy needed to calculate a generalization gap.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD with momentum against adaptive optimizers on validation accuracy.
rows.note: SGD with momentum is below all listed adaptive methods except Fromage and MSVAG, as the text states.
rows.check: Supply the missing comparator: Adam achieves 64.71±0.57 versus momentum SGD's 55.58±0.34. State that Adam's epsilon was searched while its learning rate was fixed; SGD's learning rate was searched. This is broader and asymmetric tuning relative to V4's restricted-tuning condition.

source_check.correct: Table I supplies adaptive comparators: Adam validation accuracy 64.71±0.57 versus momentum SGD 55.58±0.34. Adam's epsilon was searched with its learning rate fixed; SGD's learning rate was searched. The reversed ordering concerns this broader-tuning setting.
source_check.locator_found: Table I; Section IV.A; Appendix E, Table VII
